tasks.title: The drive's answers and redo pin: a set-aside sign-off refuses an answer by its own text, decline keeps a human's words, a blocked task's standing patch is not spent
tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R1, P155-R2, P155-R14 and P155-R15, each recorded in docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings with its file, issue and resolution. R1: a case that fails when the set-aside sign-off refusal is deleted (an --answer sign-off --reason would otherwise drive on). R2: through `next`, adding the remedy task and then answering decline --reason must keep the human's words, as decline_answer's docstring says, or the docstring and db2 change to what the drive does. R14: redo_pin_spent must not count a blocked task whose patch still stands as spent, and the stop must not name refs that were deleted. R15: sd9-sd11 must let the status arm decide a case, so `return not patch_stands` goes red. Answer each finding by id.

outcome.technical: drive-phase.py: (R14) redo_pin_spent is now `status in _mio.TERMINAL or not patch_stands`, so a blocked task keeps its pin while its patch stands; its docstring and settle_redo_pins' docstring say why (unblock hands the task back to a step that stops on the patch). redo_left gains an arm for a stop whose tree could not be read while the pin is gone: it names no `<pin>^` or `<pin>` to compare against and offers no removal of the pin. It places a `check` clause, `cd <tree> && git apply --reverse --check <patch>`, the check the patch can answer alone. I checked that command in a scratch repo: exit 0 over a tree that holds the work, exit 1 over one that lacks it. (R2) drive_locked's set-aside branch now takes `--answer decline`: for a decision set aside because a task can run, answer_refusal is asked first and refuses before the pending decision is dropped, so a decline with no --reason leaves the decision there for a second try with words. Otherwise decline_answer records the words in state['declined'], pops phaseGate, and the drive goes on to the runnable task. Every other answer is still refused with the set-aside wording. decline_answer's docstring now names this path. tests/test_drive_phase.py: rf12-rf15 in a new _rf_set_aside_answers (in _ready_first_cases), sd17 and sd18 in a new _pin_under_patch_cases (called from _scope_declared_cases), ar6g after ar6f in _recut_crash_cases. Two small helpers: _stand_patch, and _booting, lifted from _e2e_boot so both cases use one fixture. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the set-aside sentence now cites rf1 for the dispatch, rf12 for the refusal, rf13-rf15 for decline and rf2 for the blocked twin; the redo-pin sentence states the blocked-with-patch rule (sd17, sd18) and the pin-gone stop (ar6g). Mutation probes ran in a scratch copy (rsync of the worktree, __pycache__ purged between runs, an anchor count of 1 asserted, the source restored in a finally block), over the rf, sd and ar5 blocks: m1 `return not patch_stands` -> FAIL sd17 (47/48); m2 blocked counted spent again -> FAIL sd18; m3 set-aside refusal removed -> FAIL rf12; m4 decline not taken -> FAIL rf13, rf14, rf15; m5 decline refusal moved after the pop -> FAIL rf13, rf14, rf15; m6 the pin-gone arm disabled -> FAIL ar6g. Gate: python3 tools/sweep-selftests.py tests/test_drive_phase.py exit 0, '1/1 files ok, 821 cases'. ruff check on both .py files exit 0. Run in-process: _deps.doc_prose_numbers, _output_lints.prose_number_claims and house_style_violations report nothing for the touched files. Findings: P155-R1 fixed by rf12, which passes with the refusal and goes red without it (m3); it asserts exit 2, the added task's id, the set-aside wording and not 'no decision is pending', no pending in state, the phase not signed off and the task not driven; the guide cites it. P155-R2 fixed by the first option, decline taken on a set-aside decision; db2 and the docstring now describe what `next` does, and rf14 and rf15 are the drive-level cases. P155-R14 fixed both ways: the pin is kept for a blocked task (sd18), and a stop whose pin is gone names no deleted ref (ar6g). P155-R15 fixed by sd17, a cancelled task whose patch stands, so the status arm decides alone; probed with `return not patch_stands` (m1, red). Dependants: drive-phase.py's importers (_worktrees.py, test__filed_returns, test__invariants, test__worktrees, test_audit_status, test_commit_task_work, test_detect_plan_skip, test_stamp_verification) are still correct; grep for redo_pin_spent|redo_left|'is set aside: '|decline_answer|drive_locked|settle_redo_pins across tests/, tools/, plugins/ and .github/ hits only drive-phase.py and test_drive_phase.py. test_drive_phase.py's dependants: .github/sweep-costs.json is not re-recorded; the rf, sd and ar5 blocks each gained cases and so cost more than their recorded figures. The sweep's timeout is the larger of a floor and a multiple of the recorded figure, and the gate passed under it. ci.yml, tools/affected.py, tools/reach-diff.py, test__runner_output, test_run_test_gate and test_stamp_verification name the file by path or use helpers this task did not touch, so they are still correct. PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's dependants read it by basename; no tree line or section heading changed, so they are still correct.
outcome.descriptive: A set-aside sign-off decision now keeps a human's decline and its words, the refusal of other answers is pinned by a case, a blocked task keeps its redo pin while its patch stands, and a stop never names a deleted pin.

tasks.title: The drive's stop texts: one ref once, a foreign marker named as foreign, the kept-beside patch name inside the clip, every converted stop held to paths-last
tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R3, P155-R24, P155-R58, P155-R59 and P155-R75 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings), plus one found outside any finding: the unsettled_stop docstring in drive-phase.py still says ut5 names only a site reaching neither ask. R3: not_ready_why prints a blocked phase's ref twice ('waits on P9 (phase), P9'). R24: a case for the fallback wording and for a marker with a foreign createdBy, which must not read as this plugin's marker. R58: kept_beside's patch name must survive a head-keeping clip after a long relayed stop. R59: every stop converted to paths-last is held to it by a committed case (an AST walk over the _stopped calls), not only the serial redo_left branch. P155-R58: new module-level relayed_beside(ctx, stop, named, where) in drive-phase.py: the stop prefix once, then the keeping's named facts (task, patch basename), each placed clause, and the verb's own words whole as a last 'verb said' clause; the code is the verb's and ctx['stop'] (the verb's kind) is untouched. recut_tree's nested kept_beside now goes through it (keeping_said split out of keeping so both share the named sentence). kb1 drives it with a verb stop opening on a long spaced path: named facts and patch name before the first path, one prefix, verb words whole at the end, kind 'stop-lock' kept, patch name inside stop_basis(text)[:200]. P155-R59: ps1 walks the AST of drive-phase.py: every _stopped call whose words read a path-like name (_PATH_NAMES / _PATH_KEYS in the test) must be a paths_last call, or a call of a function every return of which is one (unsettled_said, keeping), or be excused in _UNROUTED_ALLOWED with its reason - one entry, follow_red_gate's follower['path'], repo-relative - and no excuse may outlive its site; ps1 also pins kept_beside routing through relayed_beside. ps2 pins the walk both ways on a planted module (bare tree and ctx['gitRoot'] named; paths_last, wrapper, pathless and excused quiet; a siteless excuse stale). Mutations, run on a scratch copy of the source text through the suite's own _unrouted_stops (no tree edit): keep_old_tree's first stop rewritten path-first -> ['keep_old_tree:5501 tree']; unsettled_said given a non-paths_last return -> ['advance_member:4910 tree', 'unsettled_stop:4864 tree']; the excuse table emptied -> ["follow_red_gate:3303 follower['path']"]; real source -> ([], []). P155-R75: the SD_LONG_ROOT comment now says only what the cases hold - spaced and nested, sd14 holds ORDER (named facts before the root's first occurrence), and no case asserts a lower length bound or names a clip width; the root's first component, which itself read 'runs long past a clip', is renamed to 'a spaced directory that stands in for a root' (one character shorter, so sd16's windows budget only loosens; sd16 green). Item outside any finding: unsettled_stop's docstring now says ut5 names a function that removes a worktree or opens a writer session without asking whether the tree is settled earlier in the source than that site, itself or through every earlier caller, and names one asking only after too (read off test__worktrees.py ut5's label). paths_last's docstring and PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md's 'A stop that carries paths' paragraph said 'Nothing checks that a new stop goes through it'; both now name ps1/ps2, their limit (a path under a name outside the case's list passes) and relayed_beside/kb1. Runs: block run `test_drive_phase.py --selftest --stage sd-block --stage ta-block` before the fix: exit 1, 54/58, FAIL ta13, nw1, kb1, ps1; after: exit 0, 58/58. tasks.title: Worktree refusals name what they will do and the tree in its native spelling, and the first-site rule has a case
tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R23, P155-R60 and P155-R68 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings), plus one found outside any finding: the exit-code line of plugins/audit/commands/worktree.md omits exit 6 (E_SETUP in manage-worktrees.py) for task-add's failed setup. R23: restore_copy's two refusals say 'the next move drops it' while unsettled_stop stops before any move; say what actually happens next. R60: ut5's first-site rule needs a planted function with two sites and an ask between them, so mutating min to max goes red. R68: native_spelling for every refusal and drive stop that names a tree (manage-worktrees' dirty and undescribable refusals and the drive stops the finding lists), through the one helper. Answer each by id.

outcome.technical: P155-R23 (restore_copy's two refusals saying 'the next move drops it'): fixed by the finding's resolution, not by rewording alone - a reworded refusal would describe a dead end, since unsettled_stop stops dispatch and integration over a standing copy before any move runs. _worktrees.restore_copy now settles both shapes the way _resume does: a copy with no index.json is dropped (new _dropped helper: restored None, the error saying the copy was dropped and the tree is settled; a drop that fails stays restored False with the copy kept); the copy of a move the marker recorded (base == end) goes to new _settle_recorded, which drops it when _newer_work over heads (end,) names nothing and otherwise keeps it naming every diverging path and saying no move, restore, dispatch or integration takes it down over newer work. The base-not-in-(start,end) refusal is unchanged. Cases un14 (no index.json dropped, tree_unsettled False after, no byte changed, HEAD at base), un15 (recorded move copy dropped, HEAD at head), un16 (over-fire twin: recorded move with newer work kept, a.txt and c.txt named, no byte changed, no 'next move' in the text). drive-phase restore_tree renders restored None as before ('nothing restored - <error>', E_USAGE), so the drop reads through it unchanged. P155-R60 (ut5's first-site and every-caller rules had no failing case): added ut6 (planted twice(): removal, tree_unsettled, second removal: named; its twin once() asking before both: not named) and ut7 (planted remover() with callers asks_first and asks_after: named; twin covered() whose two callers both ask first: not named). Proven by mutation of the scanner in a scratch exec of the test source (no file written): min to max turns ut6 red with ut5 and ut7 green; all to any turns ut7 red with ut5 and ut6 green - which also confirms the finding that ut5 alone could not tell them apart. These two cases pass on HEAD by construction because the scanner lives in the test file. P155-R68 (native_spelling only covered the unsettled family): manage-worktrees do_remove and do_task_remove now name the tree through _wt.native_spelling in every refusal naming a tree git listed - main-tree, standing-inside, not-described, dirty, and the other tasks' trees listed when none is this one's; argv and the removed field keep git's spelling. drive-phase add_tree records the tree verb's path through _worktrees.native_spelling, and every task tree the drive's state names later (wave trees, keptTrees, recuts) is that record or derived from it. Evidence for the drive half: task-add's answer was already os.path.abspath at both arms (do_task_add target, adopt_task_tree), and ntpath.abspath('C:/r/t') returns the backslash spelling (observed), so the stops the finding lists were already native in practice; add_tree now holds it whatever the verb returns. restore_copy's own messages naming the tree are spelled the same way. The finding's 'spell at the source (list_worktrees record)' was not taken: parse_list's documented contract is the path exactly as git printed it, read by modules outside this task's files (close-phase, integrate-task, panel, doctor, run-test-gate, stamp-verification), and the work order names the one helper at the refusal sites. Cases: test_manage_worktrees ns1 (windows-shaped listing, the one helper answering under ntpath for a C: path: five refusals all exit 1 and name the tree with backslashes, no forward-slash path), test_drive_phase ns1 in uy-block (git-spelled task-add answer recorded natively and submit_tree's tree-gone stop names it so). Outside any finding: plugins/audit/commands/worktree.md's exit-code line now lists 6 (E_SETUP = 6 in manage-worktrees.py, returned by provision for task-add's failed or timed-out setup; the next task-add adopts and runs the setup again, per su5a). PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md: the _worktrees section names ut6/ut7, un14-un16 and the native spelling of manage-worktrees refusals and add_tree (ns1 in each suite). Runs: the gate command exit 0 (3/3 files ok, 1084 cases); the 165 suites tools/affected.py lists for this diff through tools/sweep-selftests.py exit 0 (165/165 files ok, 16833 cases); test__refs 292/292, test__output_lints 182/182, test__deps 267/267, test__config 405/405; tools/gate-parity.py exit 0; ruff check over the six .py files exit 0; vermin -t=3.8- exit 0. Dependants: manage-worktrees.py - test__worktrees (loads it for ut1/ut2, still green), test_integrate_task (imports, green in the wide sweep), test_manage_worktrees (ns1 added), tools/affected.py (path only), PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md (updated), QUICKSTART.md (names the path only, no refusal text quoted), hooks/_config.py and require-plan.py (basename only, unchanged); worktree.md - its basename readers unchanged (name unchanged; test__refs green), CHANGELOG and docs/research unchanged; _worktrees.py - no public signature or return key changed, restore_copy is called only by drive-phase restore_tree, whose rendering of restored None is unchanged, and every importer's suite is green in the wide sweep; test__worktrees.py - new cases sit in existing blocks, _call_name/_cases/_selftest unchanged for test__affected_tests and affected.py; test_manage_worktrees.py - _g unchanged for test_drive_phase, unstaged suite; drive-phase.py - add_tree's return shape unchanged, every importer green in the wide sweep; test_drive_phase.py - no new STAGES block (ns1 joins uy-block), names read by reach-diff, run_test_gate, stamp_verification unchanged; PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md - no file added, enumeration and doc lints green (test__deps, test__config).

tasks.title: Every list flag of every audit-task verb reads one spelling: a comma-joined value is split or refused by one shared reader, never stored as one entry
tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R7, P155-R8, P155-R67 and P155-R73 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings), plus one found outside any finding: a fix task for a test-strengthening finding is created tdd with expectRedFirst although the red cannot be proved when the fix is in the test file. R73 is a class that recurred: `add --tests-add a.py,b.py` stores one entry 'a.py,b.py', and while this phase was being set up `add-phase --gate a,b,c` stored the nine gate keys as one entry (the validator only warned). The repair is one shared reader for every list-valued flag of every verb (--tests-add, --gate, --gate-add, --files, the id lists, add-phase's flags): split the same way everywhere, or refuse a value whose pieces name existing entries, never store the joined string; plus a case that walks the verbs' argparse definitions so a new list flag cannot bypass the reader. R7: the wide-gate warning must not prescribe a call that is refused without --replace. R8: --gate-add on a task with no gate of its own must not silently shrink the phase-derived gate to one entry (refuse, or seed from the entries that grade it), and the help text says which. R67: the close's evidence check must accept a files-[] task whose work is its own outputs. For the tdd item: choose the mode by where the fix lives, or make the brief say how red-first is shown for a test-file fix. Answer each by id.

tasks.title: A task's recorded gate is checked to reach the files it changes
tasks.description: Carried low findings P155-R26, P155-R32 and P155-R57 (docs/audit/phases/P155.json review.findings) are three instances of one class: a task's recorded tests.gate selects no suite that reads or runs the files the task changed (CHANGELOG/COMPATIBILITY edits graded by four suites that never open them; a verify.sh/gate-parity change graded by suites that never import it), so a passed gate run is no evidence for the change. The repair is one mechanism, not three answers: when a gate is declared or a task closes, the files the task declares (or changes) are compared with what the gate's selected suites reach, through the same reading the affected-test derivation uses, and a file no selected suite reaches is named (warning at scope time, the close records it). Past tasks' recorded gates are the record of what was run and are not rewritten; say so for each of the three findings. Answer each by id.
